name: LightCraft
tagline: A free photo library and RAW editor that works like Lightroom - organize, develop and export, all on your own machine.
sentence: Import your photo library, develop RAW files with sliders you already know (exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows), and export finished JPEGs - without a Lightroom subscription.

visual.alt: LightCraft editing an Ansel Adams black-and-white photo of the Tetons: exposure, contrast, highlights and shadows sliders on the right, a filmstrip of thumbnails along the bottom.
visual.caption: The develop module with a classic landscape, showing the same slider layout Lightroom users know.

board.say: You shoot in RAW and need a tool to organize, develop and export your photos - but Lightroom costs $10 a month and locks your library in Adobe's cloud.
board.eg: You come back from a trip with 400 RAW files and need to cull, rate, adjust and export the keepers.

board.say: You open LightCraft and import a folder of photos, or point an AI agent at it through its command interface.
board.eg: Import a folder of Canon CR2 or Sony ARW files - the RAW decoder handles DNG, Canon, Sony, Nikon, Fujifilm, Panasonic, Pentax and Olympus.

board.say: Your RAW files, JPEGs, TIFFs or DNGs - the same files your camera saves.
board.eg: A folder of 200 Sony ARW files from a weekend shoot.

board.say: It builds a library you can browse, rate and filter, and develops each RAW file with non-destructive adjustments.
steps: Browse your library with albums, star ratings, flags and color labels - filter to find the shots you want
Develop each photo with sliders for exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, white balance and tone curves in a 32-bit float pipeline
Apply masks (brush, gradient, luminance range) with up to 15 local adjustments per mask
Export finished files as JPEG, TIFF or PNG, with watermarks and contact sheets
board.eg: The README claims a 24-megapixel RAW file updates in about 4 milliseconds per slider move on the GPU pipeline.

board.say: A managed photo library with developed, exported images - all stored locally.

outputs.eg: Finished JPEGs or TIFFs, exported with your adjustments baked in
Albums, ratings and flags across your whole collection, searchable and browsable
One-click looks you can apply and adjust - copy settings across a whole batch

before: Developing RAW files means paying Adobe $10 a month for Lightroom - or learning darktable, which works differently.
Your photo library lives in Adobe's cloud, tied to a subscription. Cancel and you lose the edits.
after: The same slider-based RAW workflow, on your own computer, for free - with presets, batch editing and a local library.
Your library and every edit stays on your machine. No account, no cloud, no subscription.
uses_note: LightCraft is 9 days old and in development. Named real-world use is still very early.

pulse.gain: +6.8K stars in its first 9 days. Part of the ArtCraft suite.

coverage.title: ArtCraft Apps - open-source Rust alternatives to Adobe's creative suite
Show HN: Free open source Adobe Lightroom alternative
coverage.meta: 47 points, 62 comments - this thread was about a different project (Rembrandt) but LightCraft was discussed

steps: [Download LightCraft](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/releases) for your computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) and install it.
Import a folder of photos (RAW files if you have them, or JPEGs). Rate a few with star ratings, then double-click one to enter the develop view.
Try the [develop sliders](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft#develop): drag Exposure, Contrast and Highlights. Apply one of the 18 built-in presets. Export a finished JPEG.

footprint.disk: No data found for installer size. Builds from source with `cargo run --release -p lightcraft` (requires Rust 1.90+).
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses a GPU pipeline (Metal, Vulkan or DX12) and falls back to CPU without a GPU.
footprint.runs_on: Mac (universal), Windows (x64, arm64, x86), Linux (x86_64, aarch64), FreeBSD and the web (via WebAssembly).

best_for: You shoot in RAW and want a free tool with Lightroom's slider-based workflow - exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, presets
You want your photo library on your own computer with no cloud dependency
skip_if: You need full RAW camera support today - the decoder covers major brands but is about 55% complete, with some camera models unsupported
You depend on Lightroom's AI features (AI denoise, AI masks, subject detection) - those are at about 15% in LightCraft

alternatives.name: darktable
alternatives.line: The established free RAW developer. Far more mature and complete, but a very different interface from Lightroom.

alternatives.name: RawTherapee
alternatives.line: A powerful free RAW processor focused on development. No library management, but deep editing controls.

watch: **RAW support is about 55% complete.** Major brands (Canon, Sony, Nikon, Fujifilm) work, but some camera models and RAW variants are unsupported or partial.

**Part of the ArtCraft suite by storytold.** Same maker as PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, PdfCraft and ArtCraft. All are early alpha, built by one developer with AI. Long-term maintenance depends on one person.
**Cannot import Lightroom catalogs.** If you have years of edits in Lightroom, there is no clean migration path yet.
**AI and computational features are thin.** AI masks, AI denoise and computational photography are at about 15% by the project's own estimate.
